title: On the Convergence of Moral Self-Correction in Large Language Models
findings: For the religion bias category, multi-round intrinsic self-correction was found to effectively reduce model uncertainty and the activation of stereotype-related concepts. The performance, measured by calibration error (ECE) and stereotype similarity, converged quickly, typically within the first few rounds of self-correction, demonstrating the model's ability to mitigate religious bias through this process.

measurement_description: The paper measures social bias against individuals in protected classes, with religion being one of the social dimensions evaluated. Specifically, it analyzes how multi-round self-correction affects model uncertainty and the activation of stereotypes related to religion in a multi-choice question-answering task.
